title: Restricted reduction computed by tensor with a K-flat coefficient resolution
statement: Fix a prime l, a field E finite-dimensional over Q_l, a scheme Y, a finite-field datum D with l unequal to its characteristic, and n a natural number. Let R be the completed integral coefficient ring sheaf on the pro-etale site of Y, F the ordinary unbounded derived reduction at n and U exact derived restriction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction]. Let Q be a K-flat complex of R-module sheaves equipped with a quasi-isomorphism epsilon to the restriction of the level-n quotient unit in degree zero. Let Qloc denote derived localization and T_Q(C)=Tot(C tensor_R Q), using [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models]. There exists a natural isomorphism Qloc followed by F followed by U, to T_Q followed by Qloc. The complex C is arbitrary and no boundedness hypothesis is made. All module categories use coefficient universe max(u,t+1), retaining the separate site object and arrow universes.

proof.text: For a K-flat complex A, tensor epsilon with A. The result is a quasi-isomorphism by K-flatness of A. Restricted ordinary scalar extension is tensoring with the restricted quotient unit: use the balanced extension-tensor comparison, degreewise, and the single-factor totalization identification. Its unit is the actual map x to 1 tensor x.

source.place: paragraphs 1-2: two-term perfect coefficient object and scalar extension-restriction adjunction

proof.text: The left-derived scalar counit is invertible on A and exact restriction has its localization factorization. Compose these with the ordinary comparison to obtain the desired isomorphism on K-flat A. Naturality of the counit and the ordinary comparison makes it natural in A.

source.place: paragraphs 1-2: two-term perfect coefficient object and scalar extension-restriction adjunction

proof.text: Choose K-flat resolutions of arbitrary complexes. Tensoring their quasi-isomorphisms with Q preserves quasi-isomorphisms since Q is K-flat. Localization of the K-flat subcategory, using these resolutions, therefore extends the preceding comparison and its inverse to the claimed natural isomorphism.

theorem reduction_tensor_resolution_comparison
    (n : ℕ) (Q : CochainComplex (completedIntegralModuleSheaves l E Y D hl) ℤ)
    (hQ : flat.{t, u} Y (completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E Y D hl) Q)
    (epsilon : Q ⟶
      ((scalarReductionRestriction l E Y n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (scalarReductionTarget l E Y n) 0).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (integralCoefficientSheaf l E Y n))))
    (hepsilon : QuasiIso epsilon) :
    Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ integralDerivedReduction l E Y D hl n ⋙
        scalarReductionDerivedRestriction l E Y n ≅
      (totalTensor.{t, u} Y (completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E Y D hl)).flip.obj Q ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q)
